why: Vocabulary: blind specMult/specIndex (finsum over t ∈ (0,1) of #{i | t ∈ conjParams(e i)}) equal the project's conjMult/spectralIndex (finsum over all t, with conjParams already restricted to (0,1)) (specIndex_eq_spectralIndex). A (κ : Type): spectralIndex e = Σ_i #conjParams(e i), and doubling each eigenvalue doubles the index. B: for every finite spectrum, the conjugate parameters in (0,1) form a finite set and specIndex e = Σ_i #(conjParams(e i) ∩ (0,1)). A ⇒ B: the sum formula is A's spectralIndex_eq; the finiteness is the project's conjParams_finite (V14_7's lemma, not part of this item). B ⇒ A: spectralIndex_eq from B; spectralIndex_double then by Fintype.sum_prod_type (it is a corollary of the sum formula). Same statement.
overlap: B_to_A: only Morse.spectralIndex.eq_1 (equation lemma of the definition). A_to_B: Morse.spectralIndex.eq_1, Morse.conjParams_finite, Morse.conjParams_subset (V14_7's finiteness lemma, used for B's finiteness claim).
embedded_special_case_note: B is about the §23 matrix-group setting / spectra of K_A (concrete matrices and real numbers); it does not quantify over abstract Riemannian manifolds.
